chapters.html:
The fire in the hearth had long burned to a low amber glow, casting quiet shadows that danced across the silken drapes. The night air outside was chilly. But inside the chamber, warmth lingered. It was carried in the messy sheets, in the scent of aromatherapy herb and body fluids, and in the way their fingers remained intertwined long after their breathing had slowed.


Phainon lay half over Mydeimos, their legs tangled, his hand resting just above the new ceremonial mark below Mydeimos' navel. His thumb brushed over the edge of the red intricate design like it was sacred. No longer glowing, but still warm, pulsing faintly with the magic threaded beneath skin and bone.


“You’re warm here,” Phainon murmured, pressing a kiss onto the lower belly. “Like the mark is still whispering some spells.”


Mydeimos chuckled softly, eyes half-lidded. His golden hair splayed across the pillow, messy. “It might be. Ancient rituals tend to be a little dramatic.” His voice was hoarse, less from exertion and more from the slow-burning hours they had shared. “Isn’t that what you like? Something magical.”


Phainon grinned, his lips brushing skin again. “What I like,” he said, trailing his mouth upward, “is you.”


He kissed each rib as if it were a verse in a prayer, then moved to Mydeimos’ sternum, placing his palm there to feel the thrum of a steady heart. “Still beating,” he whispered. “Still mine. Always.”


Mydeimos turned his head, hiding his face for a moment before letting out an indulgent sigh. “You’re more sentimental than you look.”


“And you’re softer than you let anyone see,” Phainon answered, nudging his nose against Mydeimos’ jaw before kissing it.


The sheets rustled as Mydeimos turned toward him fully, one arm slinging around Phainon’s shoulders, pulling him in. The motion shifted the covers, revealing faint dusky bruises along Mydeimos' hips and some marks scattered on neck to the back, a testament to how closely they had held one another. His other hand traced down Phainon’s spine, light enough to tease while Phainon bit another space on the shoulder.


“You keep marking me,” he said, almost a whisper.


Phainon looked down at him, caught between apology and pride. “I like knowing I was here. Also these are the reminders of what happened.”


Mydeimos raised an eyebrow. “As if I could forget. I don’t think there’s a single place in this room that hasn’t seen us.”


A grin tugged at Phainon’s mouth, almost smug. “You didn’t complain even when I pinned you against the window.”


“I did complain,” Mydeimos replied dryly. “I said the glass was cold. You misinterpreted it as enthusiasm and thrust faster.”


Phainon laughed, brushing back damp strands from Mydeimos' forehead. “Still, you didn't say you don't like it.”


Mydeimos scoffed, but he didn't deny. “You’re getting bolder.”


Phainon kissed him again, sweet and tender. “Well, nevertheless, I’d remember everything,” he murmured against his lips. “Every sound you made. Every place you trembled. Every time you pulled me closer.”


“...You were different tonight though,” Mydeimos whispered. His thumb brushed along the edge of Phainon’s jaw. “You’ve always loved me fiercely, but tonight... this was a bit different.”


"Different how?"


"You're softer."


"Does that mean you like it rough?" Mydeimos' visage slightly turned brighter at the question.


"I didn't say that... Just harmless question."


Phainon chuckled, kissed his husband's knuckle.

“Well maybe it’s because it wasn’t just desire. I’ve wanted you for so long but tonight, I was loving you for a future. For something we’re building.” He rested his forehead against Mydeimos'. “This body of mine. This room. Or even this kingdom. I want all of it to feel like home for you. For us. For our future child. Even when the world expected a lot from you, I want you to be at ease when we're together.”


The intimacy of those words made Mydeimos' breath caught in throat. He didn’t respond with more vows, he didn’t need to. Instead, he tugged Phainon down for another kiss, one that deepened with every breath, with every slow shift of body against body beneath the blanket.


Although neither of them moved with urgency, the heat kindled again. Less like fire, more like slow sunrise, inching across skin with golden fondness.


Phainon’s kisses trailed lower again, and Mydeimos' fingers curled in the sheets. “It’s still morning,” he murmured, but made no move to stop him.


“Exactly,” Phainon said with the voice which already darkened with affection. “Still time to worship you properly.”


And so he did, again and again, until what they could hear was only their harmonious voices in pleasure.

Phainon and Caelus were at an orphanage, playing baseball with the kids during a charity event when a messenger came. He informed them that Mydeimos just returned from the border a week faster than intended because he fainted. Phainon's brain stopped thinking instantly. Caelus shouted something when Phainon dashed off the orphanage field but he hadn’t heard it over the buzzing panic in his skull. He kept running, faster and faster, 'till he reached the castle gate.


The halls blurred, golden sconces and dusky banners whipping past as Phainon made his way through, breath caught somewhere between his lungs and his heart. The echo of his footsteps bounced wildly off marble. 


Mydeimos was never unwell. Not once. Not even when everyone else collapsed from exhaustion, not even when blades grazed his ribs. Not even when grief tore him apart. The news had made Phainon’s blood run cold, and worse, his mind had leapt ahead, racing through a thousand terrible possibilities.


Perhaps someone found out Mydeimos' weakness.

Perhaps the immortality granted to him had an invisible price.

Phainon was scared, he was beyond terrified.


He skidded around the last turn, nearly slamming into a bewildered attendant.

“Out of the way,” he muttered breathlessly, flinging open the grand doors of the royal bedchamber.


The heavy scent of incense and medicine wrapped around him like a shroud.


“Mydei—” he choked, but the rest of his words crumbled in his throat.


Hephaestion was there, standing with arms crossed by the window, his brows were knitted like he was in deep thought. Perdikkas, by contrast, was kneeling beside the bed, his hand gentle against the sleeping king’s pulse. Mydeimos lay across the sheets, stripped of his ceremonial garments and glistening with sweat. His brows drawn and lips slightly parted as if whispering fevered words even in sleep.


Phainon’s eyes widened in horror. He didn’t even realize he had the baseball glove clutched in one hand until it thudded softly to the floor.


"Your highness..." Hephaestion bowed formally, followed by Perdikkas. But Phainon didn't answer after it.


“What happened?” His voice cracked on the second word. “Why does he look so pale? What’s wrong with him?”


The two aides exchanged a loaded glance. Hephaestion looked away as if to shift the responsibility. Perdikkas, looked a little unsure but he decided to take it, straightened his body before he faced the agitated Queen.


“The king is not in danger,” he said carefully.


“That’s not an answer,” Phainon snapped, stepping closer to the bed, ignoring the trembling in his knees. “Tell me what’s wrong. He's not just anyone who could faint without reason.”


"It's not like I don't want to answer but..." Perdikkas pressed his lips into a tight line. “Perhaps it would be better if Mydeimos told you himself.”


Phainon’s hands curled into fists. He was about to retort when the soft sound of cloth shifting made him freeze.


“You’re being so loud, Phainon,” came Mydeimos’ hoarse, dry voice, barely above a whisper but enough to pierce through the haze in Phainon’s mind.


“Mydei—” Phainon surged forward just as Perdikkas reached to help the king sit up. Sweat clung to his hairline, and his skin, though flushed, had some of its color returned. His golden eyes blinked open slowly, groggy but focused enough to land on Phainon.


“Calm down,” Mydeimos murmured, rasping as he leaned into the pillow. “I’m not dying.”


Phainon didn’t answer. He was already at the bedside, falling to his knees, taking Mydeimos' hand in both of his and holding it tightly, scanning every inch of exposed skin as if searching for hidden wounds.


“You scared me,” he whispered. “What happened? The messenger said you fainted...”


Mydeimos' fingers squeezed his gently.


Behind them, Hephaestion and Perdikkas exchanged a subtle nod. Mydeimos gestured faintly, and without a word, the two aides made their quiet exit, leaving only the sound of the door easing shut behind them.


“Sit,” Mydeimos said softly, patting the edge of the mattress.


Phainon obeyed, knuckles white as he held onto Mydeimos' hand, barely able to speak through the pressure blooming in his chest.


“I don’t want you to panic,” Mydeimos began, his voice calm but calculated, like he was weighing something so serious. “But I want you to hear everything from me. Don't blame those two for not answering."


"Alright," Phainon swallowed, “okay, just... Please tell me. Is everything okay? Are you okay?”


There was a pause.


Then, Mydeimos tilted his head, the shadow of something flickering behind his eyes, nervous but it didn't seem like anything rooting from fear, not quite.


“You’re going to be a father,” he said, softly. 


"Huh..?"


“I’m pregnant.”


The words struck like an earthquake. Phainon blinked once, twice. “You—what?”


“I’m carrying our child.”


Phainon’s mouth opened. Closed. Opened again. A rush of breath escaped him like someone had knocked the wind from his lungs. For a moment, he said nothing—no sound, no movement—until finally he managed a strangled:


“Y, you’re not joking?”


“I wouldn’t collapse in front of my cavalry unit just to make a joke."


Phainon stared at him, wide-eyed and pale, and then suddenly he laughed, high and thin and cracking midway.


“I, see... You're pregnant. Haha, we did it..."


“Yeah, we did it,” Mydeimos replied with a soft chuckle. “Congratulation.”


"Don't make it sound like my only achievement." Phainon’s hand moved involuntarily to Mydeimos' abdomen, hovering there, hesitant. "How are you feeling now?"


"I'm fine. Just a bit tired." Mydeimos leaned back into the pillows, eyes half-lidded but still watching him. “I already had the feeling when my stomach acted a bit odd these past weeks. Confirmed it this morning. Perdikkas ran tests twice.”


“Is it safe?” Phainon whispered, his hand finally landing gently over the tummy, gently stroked it beneath the linen. "Are you safe?"


Mydeimos covered his hand with his own. “For now. But I’m not allowed to ride a horse, spar, or skip meals anymore. Perdikkas is turning into a strict monster.”


“Sorry, but I’ll help the monster,” Phainon said immediately, earnestly. “I’ll cook. I’ll tie your boots. I’ll guard you from your own bad habits.”


Mydeimos arched a brow. “Will you guard me from the mountain of scrolls waiting in my study?”


“...I can hide them?”


That earned a breathless chuckle. Phainon leaned forward and pressed his forehead against the back of Mydeimos' hand.


“I thought I was going to lose you,” he admitted. “I was so scared..."


“I’m not going anywhere,” Mydeimos murmured, tone dropped softer now. “Not when there’s a part of you growing inside me.”


Phainon leaned up, kissing him, easing the fear he hadn’t dared to name and the joy he didn’t yet know how to hold.


Somewhere behind them, the wind tugged gently at the velvet curtains, and far below, the court still bustled with its rhythms. But here in the hush of the royal chamber, nothing else mattered.


Only the two of them, and what now bloomed between.

The study had become something between a war room and a private lounge. Tall windows let in the late morning light, casting honey-gold stripes across the stone floor and shelves burdened with scrolls. And in the middle of it, Mydeimos reclined sideways on the velvet-lined chaise, one arm tucked beneath his head. A fine wool blanket rested across his legs, though it had slipped to reveal the curve of his belly. Barely past two months, but visible enough beneath the folds of his tunic. His brows furrowed in concentration as he scanned the parchment in his hand.

On the floor beside the chaise sat Phainon, barefoot, dressed far too casually for someone supposedly aiding in state matters. His sleeves were rolled up past his elbows, and his hands were firmly on task. His thumbs working slow, deliberate circles into the arch of Mydei’s foot, kneading out tension with practiced focus.

Across the room, the five trusted aides had clustered around the long table, minding their own business...or at least, tried to. Ptolemy muttered something about taxes. Leonnius was half-distracted, glancing between his report and the scene by the chaise. Hephaestion merely smirked as he sorted through some letters. Perdikkas jotted down something in his medical ledger. Peucesta plucked a quiet note from the lyre resting on his knee, playing a gentle tune just to fill the silence.

“The northern lords still haven't responded to the new tariffs,” Hephaestion said at last.

“Send another letter,” Mydeimos replied, not looking up. “Use firmer phrasing.”

“You mean your usual brand of barely veiled threats?” Perdikkas asked without glancing up from his notes.

Mydeimos arched a brow. “It works most of time.”

“They do,” Ptolemy admitted, pushing his spectacles further up his nose, “but diplomacy, they say, is the art of saying ‘nice dog’ while reaching for a rock.”

Phainon snorted, reaching over to pick up a slice of fruit from the silver tray on the side table. “That sounds like something you’d write in your book.”

“It is,” Ptolemy admitted proudly. "Book two, chapter nine!"

Phainon shook his head. “Mydei, open your mouth,” he then murmured to Mydeimos.

The king narrowed his eyes. “I’m not a child.”

“You’re pregnant and distracted,” Phainon grinned, holding the slice of persimmon teasingly close. “Which means I’m winning.”

Mydeimos gave him a look that almost like a warning in a hundred silent ways but opened his mouth anyway. The fruit disappeared between his lips, and his expression twitched in reluctant pleasure.

"Yummy?"

"Mm, I guess so."

"Okay, here comes the next one. Aaah?"

Across the room, Leonnius cleared his throat. “Ahem… about the envoy from the Southernmost Isle?”

“They arrive next week,” Mydeimos answered, still chewing. “Make sure their chambers are prepared. No incense, they get headaches.”

“Already arranged,” Leonnius replied. “I also doubled the guard.”

“And the menu?” Mydeimos added.

“I gave the chef a list.”

Phainon, still calmly massaging his husband’s calf, leaned up with another slice of fruit. “Ready?”

“No,” Mydeimos muttered, and yet another piece vanished just as easily.

"Oops, the juice dripped, let me just..." Phainon wiped the liquid with his thumb and licked it off. "There, all clean."

Hephaestion sighed, as loud as he could. “Do you two want the room?”

“I’d say yes,” Phainon said cheerfully. “But then we’d have to do the paperwork later, and you all keep finding ways to sneak the boring parts to Mydei.”

“Because he actually reads them,” Perdikkas said flatly.

“And because he's terrifying,” Ptolemy added. “Especially when he doesn’t get things done in his way.”

“I'm still here,” Mydeimos murmured.

“I know. I said it so you'll realize what kind of perfectionist you can be.” Ptolemy said with zero repentance.

Mydeimos shifted on the chaise, sitting down whilst grunting under his breath as his lower back tensed. Phainon, already anticipating it, repositioned himself and began tracing soothing circles just around his husband's spine.

“You’re spoiling him,” Hephaestion noted.

“Gladly,” Phainon replied without missing a beat. “He carries the heir. The least I can do is carry everything else.”

“Like the fruit tray?” Mydeimos asked dryly.

“Exactly,” Phainon beamed. “You finally understand.”

Mydeimos rolled his eyes, yet his fingers had unconsciously reached down to brush lightly against Phainon’s hand. The room once again filled with rustling papers and reports.

But even in the middle of strategic debate, their rhythm was unshaken. Like Mydeimos tilted his head back, one hand resting lightly on the swell of his belly, and Phainon leaned in just to press a fleeting kiss to his forehead and whispered for his husband to not tire himself out.

None of the aides said a word. They merely exchanged glances that said, Well. This is our life now.

The talk continued, escalated. From preparation to welcome a delegate and eventually moving to most concerned point. Safety. After all, Kremnos had a lot of enemies. Some foolishly challenged. They put the pregnancy news as ailment, not knowing that the lion might be more fierce while carrying, and his spouse might be even worse.

Maps were stretched over desk now, annotated with red brush marks and thin trails like veins, tracing troop movements and territories soaked in years of conflict. 

Perdikkas pointed at a gorge outlined in ochre. “If we destroy the canyon walls here, their supply caravan will be trapped. It’ll seal their route for the season, at least.”

Leonnius frowned. “It will bury them alive.”

“Yes,” Perdikkas answered, unfazed. “That’s the point.”

Phainon was staring at the map with growing unease, until suddenly, his palm landed firmly against Mydeimos' belly. “We are not talking about this in front of the baby.”

The room paused. Peucesta blinked slowly. Ptolemy’s pen hovered mid-air. Even Mydeimos looked at him.

“It’s a two-months old fetus,” Hephaestion muttered, unimpressed. “It doesn’t understand siege tactics.”

“We don’t know that!” Phainon snapped, adjusting his protective hover. “They say the child absorbs what they heard. Do you want our royal baby to come out and immediately planning a counterattack?!"

“That is the child of a warlord, for sure.” Ptolemy said thoughtfully, flipping open his notebook. “‘And thus the heir stirred, forged in the womb not of silk, but of stratagem.’” He looked up. “That’s going in the next chapter.”

“Leave the unborn alone, Ptolemy,” Phainon grumbled.

“I’m just documenting history, Your Majesty.”

Perdikkas, calm as ever, sipped his tea. “You were the one who came up with this exact avalanche strategy three campaigns ago.”

“That was before Mydei was pregnant!”

Leonnius tilted his head. “Two months ago?”

“Exactly. I’ve changed.” Phainon puffed his chest and gestured proudly to Mydei’s stomach. “I’m nurturing now. I care about energies. Vibes. Womb tranquility.”

Mydeimos rolled his eyes skyward.

Hephaestion raised a brow. “Dear Queen, you literally said last week we should spike their water supplies.”

“That was post-midnight, I was sleep-deprived and emotional.”

“Because the bakery ran out of sweetbread,” Ptolemy added helpfully.

“You try denying a pregnant monarch his sugar intake,” Phainon huffed. “Do you know what he did? He gave me the death glare. I’d rather face a cavalry charge.”

“You’re the only one panicking,” Mydeimos muttered, attempting to return to the scroll in front of him.

“Oh, I’m so sorry to be the only one who cares. But don't you all not see the way my husband glows? He’s radiant. And pregnant. And still running a kingdom. Someone has to worry.”

“And naturally, that someone is the man who suggested catapulting severed body parts into enemy's camp five days ago,” Hephaestion said.

“It was a symbolic gesture!”

“Of horror,” Peucesta finally added, softly, with that deceptively calm voice of his. "Sometimes, I feel our Queen is far more ruthless than our King."

"I know, right?" Hephaestion shrugged. "He insisted to take over the meeting a week ago and I've never seen someone outsmarted the old folks and left them all speechless."

"By all respect, our queen is terrifying, especially when dueling with words. He's ruthless." Leonnius also chirped, with newfound adoration. "He even more scarier with blade in hand."

"That's...a compliment, right?" Phainon glanced at Mydeimos, which his husband only answered with a shrug of shoulder.

“Okay, still! My point stands,” Phainon continued, one hand still possessively on Mydeimos’ bump. “Can we please just skip the scary murder avalanche plan and talk about safer things like treaties? Trade, maybe?”

Leonnius looked at him, thoughtful. “Like how you once suggested using enemy merchants as bait.”

Phainon raised his eyebrows. “How do you all remember this much?”

Mydeimos rubbed his temple. “Because you never stop bringing grotesque idea to the table.”

"I just thought that some people didn't deserve mercy..."

Ptolemy, pen already scratching furiously, added, “‘And lo, the father-to-be became the kingdom’s loudest guardian. Bearing no blade, only concern and unsolicited opinions.’”

“Ptolemy.”

“Don’t worry, I’ll frame it flatteringly.”

Phainon huffed and leaned into Mydeimos' space. “Just say the word and I’ll haul you back to bed with a tower of blankets. You don’t need this stress.”

“I’m fine,” Mydeimos said. “You are the stress.”

Phainon squinted. “...Fair.”

Still, when the conversation returned to military logistics and difficult choices, Phainon’s hand never left Mydei’s belly. He sat a little straighter. Watched a little more quietly. Every time the word blood or ambush came up, his thumb rubbed a little circle just under the king’s ribs.

However, somewhere between documents and decisions, it had become clearer: Mydei and Phainon weren’t simply ruling together, they were existing together. Clashing and fitting in all the right places. Equal and opposite, yet impossibly entwined.

Kremnos would not fall while these two ruled. Not with this much bickering and affection.

chapters.title: Dictating Nation and Craving
chapters.html:
The season had turned. Summer’s bright cruelty softened into autumn blush. Outside the windows of the royal chamber, the garden rustled with dry leaves and the scent of damp earth. But inside, the morning was far less serene.


"Hyacine!" Phainon’s groan echoed from behind the partitioned screen. "I swear if this is divine punishment, just say it, I’ll accept it with grace and throw myself off to the altar."


The Queen's private physician blinked as she stepped into the antechamber, tray in hand. "We’ve discussed this, your highness. No self-flinging until at least after midday," Hyacine said dryly, setting down a warm bowl of ginger broth. "Besides, I doubt the Titans would go through the trouble of blessing your union just to curse your stomach."


Phainon slumped back against the pillows, his face an unflattering shade between pale pearl and seafoam green. One arm was dramatically slung over his eyes, the other curled around a ceramic basin that had seen too much action in the last few weeks.


"This has to be a joke," he muttered hoarsely. "There’s no womb in me. I did not receive the ritual. Why am I the one throwing up every morning?"


"I’d like to know that too," came Mydeimos' voice, calmer as ever. He stood near the foot of the bed, already dressed in a simple robe of heavy draped linen, the front of it stretched gently by a four-month bump that he carried, yet he still looked so regal. His golden eyes flicked toward Phainon, concerned.


"You’re not the one carrying a future heir," Mydeimos continued, arms crossed as he shifted his weight. "I should be the one groaning over chamber pots, not you."


Phainon peeked through his fingers, then squinted up at his husband. "Do not take this from me. Let me suffer for you. I swore to protect and help you through everything, didn’t I? This must be it. My body, somehow protesting what I did to yours."


"You mean ramming like a mad beast until I couldn’t walk straight for three days?" Mydeimos raised a brow. "Truly, a crime."


Hyacine coughed, as if to remind the royal couple about her presence here.


Phainon groaned louder. "I just wanted to make sure that I impregnated you right..."


"What does that even mean..."

"It means I love you and I am dying."


"You’re not." Despite himself, Mydeimos smiled, just faintly. He moved to sit at the edge of the bed, brushing the damp hair back from Phainon’s forehead. "Both Perdikkas and Hyacine already checked. There is nothing wrong with you."


"I smell bad."


"No, you don't."


"You're making fun of me..."


Mydeimos sighed, brushing a thumb across his husband's cheek. "I’m not making fun of you. I just don’t understand why it’s you, not me."


Hyacine, setting down a vial of herbs near the table, smiling so sweetly. "There are recorded cases. Rare, but not impossible. Bonded partners sometimes experience sympathetic symptoms. Especially when the connection is strong."


"You’re saying I love him so much that I’m vomiting on his stead?"


"That’s... one way to phrase it," Hyacine's smile turned wry as she adjusted the covers and tried not to think too deeply.


Phainon exhaled heavily, then looked down at Mydeimos' belly. His eyes softened immediately.


He reached forward and laid his head against the slight swell. His cheek pressed against the warm fabric of the robe, and one hand rose to stroke across the bump with slow fingers. The motion wasn’t graceful. It was clumsy, still unsure but it carried gentleness and affection.


“Hey,” he mumbled to the child within, softly, almost sheepish. “Take it easy on your parents, will you?”


Mydeimos arched a brow but said nothing. His hand instinctively moved to Phainon’s hair, combing through it lazily.


“Well, if you’re gonna kick or scream or demand attention,” Phainon went on, “keep throwing it all my way, alright? The king has enough to handle. I’ll handle the rest. Even if its being nauseous every day.”


Before Mydeimos could retort, the chamber doors burst open after two knocks. Caelus strode in, far too energetic for the hour, followed by two warmly familiar figures trailing behind him.


“Good morning, your majesties!” Caelus greeted brightly. “And look who I found wandering through the city gates asking for their way to the palace.”


“Mother! Father!” Phainon brightened immediately, scrambling up with unsteady legs.


Audata, still with her kindhearted smile, approached Mydeimos instead.


“You’re glowing, dear! The pregnancy turned you even prettier.” she said warmly, cupping Mydeimos’ cheeks before placing her hand gently over the bump. “How are you feeling?”


“Far better than my husband,” Mydeimos said with a chuckle. “It’s good to see you again, Mother.”


Hieronymus gave a quiet chuckle from beside her. “You’re keeping well, then?”


“Well enough, Father,” Mydeimos said. “Though I’ve officially been barred from leading any excursions beyond the palace.”


"That's good." Hieronymus nodded approvingly. "Pregnancy is not easy. You need to take a rest."


"Right. Don't push yourself too hard, Mydeimos." Audata added, stroking the bump fondly.


Phainon groaned. “Meanwhile, I’m half a ghost.”


Audata turned to him with a slow blink. “Forgive me, who are you again?”


“What? Mom! It's me!"


"Who?"


"I'm your only son, Phainon!”


"Weird..." Audata placed a palm over her cheek, lips pursed in thought. “I remember a sweet son of mine named Mydeimos who sent letters every fortnight. I don’t recall raising one who only remembers his parents exist after being scolded by his husband.”


“Haha, you're so petty, mom. You know writing is not my favourite thing to do.”


Audata sighed with exasperated affection, brushing back Phainon’s hair as if he were still a child who scraped his knees. “Still as pathetic as the day you were born.”


"Excuse me?!"


Hieronymus finally stepped forward, patting Phainon’s shoulder. “She doesn’t mean it, son.”


“I absolutely do,” Audata said.


Phainon slumped in exaggerated defeat, leaning back against Mydeimos again. “You see what I grew up with?"


Audata laughed, and something eased between all of them. The room warmed, not from sunlight, but from familiarity.


“Oh, and by the way,” Audata said, wiping a bit of imaginary dust from the edge of Mydeimos’ sleeve, “when I was carrying Phainon, it was his father who had the morning sickness.”
